1065: Even if it is only porridge as thin as clear water, nothing is sweeter than food you have earned with your own hard work.
1066: Even if you beg only for water for a thirsty cow, nothing is more shameful for your tongue than begging.
1067: I beg everyone who begs: if you must beg, never beg from people who hide what they have.
1075: Fear is the only thing that makes mean people behave well. Beyond that, they behave a little better only when they want something.
1077: After eating, mean people will not even shake the leftover grains off their wet hand for anyone, except for those who would break their jaw with a fist.
1081: Is she a goddess, a lovely peacock, or a human girl wearing heavy earrings? My heart is confused and cannot tell.
1097: Little harsh words that hold no anger, and looks like an enemy's, are signs of people who love each other while acting like strangers.
1107: Holding this lovely young woman feels like living in your own home and eating food you earned yourself, after sharing it with others.
1111: Anicham flower (a flower so delicate it wilts if you just smell it), long may you live! You are truly soft, but the one I love is even softer than you.
1114: If the blue water lilies could see her, they would hang their heads and stare at the ground, saying, 'We cannot match the eyes of this girl with fine jewels.'
1129: I know that if I blink he will be hidden, so I keep my eyes open. For that reason alone, this town says he does not love me.
1131: For those who suffer and are hurt by love, there is no protection and no strength except the madal. That is a horse of palm stems that a refused lover rides in public.
1133: Once I had modesty and a man's honor. Today all I have is the palm-stem horse that lovesick men ride.
1134: The wild flood of love sweeps away the raft made of modesty and a man's honor.
1140: People with no understanding laugh at me right in front of my eyes, only because they have never suffered what I suffer.
1163: In my body, which cannot bear it any longer, love and modesty hang from the two ends of a carrying pole. My very life is that pole.
1183: He took away my beauty and my modesty. In return, he gave me love-sickness and this paleness.
1194: Even a woman loved by many is truly unlucky if the one she loves does not love her back.
